imported.definition: Brought into a country from another country to be sold.
imported.example: Ever since tea was first imported to Great Britain from China

colonies.definition: Lands ruled by a faraway country and settled by people from it.
colonies.example: they brought this habit with them to their colonies in North America

colonists.definition: People who live in a colony, a land ruled by a faraway country.
colonists.example: In the British colonies of North America, colonists did not like having to pay such high prices.

government.definition: The group of people who make the laws and run a country.
government.example: the British government made a special deal with the East India Company

monopoly.definition: When only one company is allowed to sell something, so no one else can compete.
monopoly.example: They granted the East India Company a monopoly on tea

smugglers.definition: People who secretly bring goods in or out of a place against the law.
smugglers.example: they turned to Dutch smugglers, who sneaked in tea that was just as good

smuggled.definition: Brought in secretly against the law.
smuggled.example: English tea was cheaper than smuggled Dutch tea

sneaked.definition: Moved or brought something quietly so no one would notice.
sneaked.example: they turned to Dutch smugglers, who sneaked in tea that was just as good

expensive.example: Lead, glass, paints, and paper all became more expensive.

taxes.definition: Money that people pay to the government to help pay for public services.
taxes.example: government taxes made the cost of tea even higher

tax.definition: Money paid to the government, which uses it to pay for services for the people.
tax.example: the Townshend tax was still in effect

taxing.example: referring to the government taxing people without their consent

unpopular.example: after the incredibly unpopular Stamp Act of 1765

tradition.definition: A way of doing things that has been kept for a long time.
tradition.example: According to the British tradition, a tax could only be enacted

parliament.definition: The group of people who make a country's laws, as in Great Britain.
parliament.example: Parliament agreed and passed a series of acts in 1767

representatives.definition: People chosen to speak and vote for other people.
representatives.example: But the colonists didn't have any representatives in Parliament.

representation.definition: Having someone speak and vote for you in government.

consent.example: referring to the government taxing people without their consent

merchants.definition: People who buy and sell goods.

economy.definition: All the buying, selling, and making of things in a country.

principle.definition: A basic belief about what is right and what is wrong.
principle.example: It was a question of principle

violation.definition: The breaking of a rule or law.

outraged.definition: Very angry about something that seems unfair.

protestors.definition: People who show in public that they disagree with something.

disguised.definition: Dressed or made to look like someone else so no one knows who you are.

harbor.definition: A sheltered place by the sea where ships can stay safely.

fortune.definition: A very large amount of money.

declaration.example: the Declaration of Independence was signed

independence.definition: Freedom from being ruled by another country.
